behavior.basis: real JO-subtype -> giant fiber synapses (FlyWire FAFB v783, 830 synapses across 4 JO subtypes, pair-verified) + classic giant fiber escape literature; stated pathway role is known biology, edges are measured
behavior.text: Noxious startle/escape: sharp mechanosensory input to the antennae drives Johnston's organ mechanoreceptors, which synapse directly on the giant fiber neuron, triggering the jump-and-flight escape reflex. The fly's pain-equivalent pathway.

honest_note: Adult nociceptive-LABELED classes (FBbt_00051492, FBbt_00048471) are not indexed with usable connectivity in any reachable form (see GAPS.md §7) — this chain is the REAL noxious-mechanosensory -> giant-fiber escape pathway, the fly's functional pain-equivalent circuit: a sharp mechanical insult drives antennal Johnston's organ mechanoreceptors -> the giant fiber startle neuron -> thoracic escape motor. Presented as the nociceptive-functional pathway, NOT as labeled pain neurons.

source: Virtual Fly Brain VFBquery HTTP API (https://v3-cached.virtualflybrain.org/), FlyWire FAFB v783 connectome. Hop 0->1 edges: per-pair /query_connectivity (upstream_type=<JO subtype class>, downstream_type='giant fiber neuron'), edge weight = summed synapse count across verified neuron pairs; discovered via UpstreamClassConnectivity of the giant fiber neuron (FBbt_00004020), which returned mechanosensory classes upstream. Hop 1->2 edges: class-aggregated /query_connectivity downstream of the giant fiber neuron, edge weight = total synapse count. All rows real; nothing invented.
